board_events.text: A classical electron in orbit is an accelerating charge, and accelerating charges radiate energy.
So the electron should bleed energy continuously, spiral inward, and crash into the nucleus in about $10^{-8}$ s.
Two things are wrong at once: atoms are STABLE, and they emit only a few sharp colours.
The planetary atom was elegant and completely wrong about how atoms actually behave.
Something inside the atom refuses to obey classical physics. That is the puzzle Bohr walks into.

segments.text: We open Part two with a genuine crisis in physics, and it is worth feeling the weight of it, because Bohr's whole model is a response to this crisis.

By nineteen twelve, Rutherford had handed physics a beautiful picture: a nuclear atom, with electrons orbiting a tiny dense central nucleus, held by Coulomb attraction, exactly the way planets orbit the sun. Elegant, intuitive, and, as it turns out, fatally broken.

Look at the spiral. Here is the mechanism that destroys it. An electron moving in a circular orbit is constantly changing direction, so it is accelerating. And electromagnetic theory is completely unambiguous on this: an accelerating charge radiates energy away.

So a classical orbiting electron cannot hold its orbit. It bleeds energy continuously, spirals inward faster and faster, and crashes into the nucleus in about ten to the power minus eight seconds. A hundred-millionth of a second.

That alone is a disaster. Every atom in your body should have collapsed almost instantly after forming. They plainly have not. Matter is stubbornly, obstinately stable, and the planetary model cannot explain why.

And there is a second failure sitting right beside it. When atoms are energised and emit light, they emit only a few sharp, specific colours, never the smooth continuous rainbow a spiralling electron would produce as its frequency changed.
So the planetary atom is elegant and completely wrong about how atoms behave. It gets the geometry right and the physics catastrophically wrong.

<curious>Which leaves us with a strange conclusion. Something inside the atom simply refuses to obey classical physics. That is the puzzle Bohr walks straight into, and his response is one of the boldest moves in the history of the subject.
Part दो की शुरुआत physics के एक सच्चे संकट से करते हैं, और इसका वज़न महसूस करना ज़रूरी है, क्योंकि Bohr का पूरा model इसी संकट का जवाब है।

उन्नीस सौ बारह तक Rutherford ने physics को एक सुंदर तस्वीर दी थी: एक nuclear atom, जिसमें electrons एक छोटे dense central nucleus के चारों ओर घूमते हैं, Coulomb attraction से बँधे, ठीक जैसे planets सूरज के गिर्द। सुंदर, सहज, और जैसा निकला — घातक रूप से टूटा हुआ।

spiral देखिए। यही वो mechanism है जो इसे तोड़ता है। circular orbit में घूमता electron लगातार direction बदल रहा है, यानी accelerate कर रहा है। और electromagnetic theory इस पर बिलकुल साफ़ है: accelerating charge energy radiate करता है।

तो classical orbiting electron अपनी orbit रख ही नहीं सकता। वो लगातार energy खोता है, तेज़ी से अंदर spiral करता है, और करीब दस की घात माइनस आठ seconds में nucleus में गिर जाता है। सेकंड का एक करोड़वाँ हिस्सा।
अकेले यही एक आपदा है। आपके शरीर का हर atom बनते ही लगभग तुरंत ढह जाना चाहिए था। साफ़ है कि ऐसा नहीं हुआ। matter ज़िद्दी तरीक़े से stable है, और planetary model बता नहीं सकता क्यों।

और इसके ठीक बग़ल में एक दूसरी failure बैठी है। जब atoms energise होकर light छोड़ते हैं, तो वो सिर्फ़ कुछ तेज़, ख़ास colours छोड़ते हैं — कभी वो smooth continuous rainbow नहीं जो spiral करता electron अपनी बदलती frequency के साथ देता।
तो planetary atom सुंदर है और atom के बर्ताव के बारे में पूरी तरह ग़लत। geometry सही पकड़ता है, physics बुरी तरह ग़लत।

<curious>इससे एक अजीब निष्कर्ष निकलता है। atom के अंदर कुछ classical physics मानने से साफ़ इनकार कर देता है। यही वो पहेली है जिसमें Bohr सीधे घुसते हैं, और उनका जवाब इस विषय के इतिहास की सबसे बोल्ड चालों में से एक है।

sections.title: Bohr's move: the ramp becomes a staircase

board_events.text: New rules, written down by hand
In 1913 Niels Bohr decided the rules of classical physics simply do not apply inside the atom, and wrote down new ones.

board_events.caption: Continuous energies versus quantised energies

board_events.text: A car-park RAMP lets you stop at any height: a continuous range of energies.
A STAIRCASE lets you stand only on a step: height one, height two, three, never half a step.
Classical physics treated the electron like the ramp. Bohr declared the atom is a staircase.
The electron may occupy only certain special orbits with certain fixed energies, and nothing in between.
This is a postulate, not a derivation. Bohr assumed it because it worked, and justified it later.

segments.text: Faced with that crisis, Bohr did something audacious. In nineteen thirteen, a young Dane who had worked briefly in Rutherford's own lab decided that the rules of classical physics simply do not apply inside the atom, and he wrote down new rules by hand.

That is worth pausing on. He did not derive these rules from something deeper. He postulated them, because they produced the right answers, and left the justification for later. This is physics being done boldly.
The picture to hold is a car park. Compare the ramp of a multi-storey car park with the staircase of the same building. Look at both in the diagram.

On the ramp, you can stop your scooter at absolutely any height you like. It is a continuous range. This is how classical physics treated the electron: any orbit allowed, any energy allowed, a smooth continuum.
On the staircase, you can only stand on a step. Height one, height two, height three, and never half a step in between. The allowed positions are discrete, separated, countable.

And Bohr's declaration is exactly this: the atom is a staircase, not a ramp. The electron may occupy only certain special orbits, each with its own certain fixed energy, and nothing whatsoever in between them.

That single idea kills both classical failures at a stroke. If the electron can only sit on fixed steps, there is a lowest step it cannot fall below, so the atom is stable. And energy can only be emitted in the fixed jumps between steps, which is why the colours are sharp.
So keep the word postulate firmly in mind. Bohr assumed the staircase. He did not prove it. And for now that is enough, because what matters next is which orbits count as the allowed steps.

उस संकट के सामने Bohr ने एक दुस्साहसी काम किया। उन्नीस सौ तेरह में, एक जवान Dane जो थोड़े समय Rutherford की ही lab में काम कर चुका था, उसने तय किया कि atom के अंदर classical physics के नियम लागू ही नहीं होते, और उसने हाथ से नए नियम लिख डाले।

यहाँ रुकना ज़रूरी है। उन्होंने ये नियम किसी गहरी चीज़ से derive नहीं किए। उन्होंने इन्हें postulate किया, क्योंकि ये सही जवाब देते थे, और justification बाद के लिए छोड़ दिया। यही physics को बोल्ड तरीक़े से करना है।
जो तस्वीर पकड़नी है वो है एक car park। एक multi-storey car park की ramp की तुलना उसी building की staircase से कीजिए। दोनों को diagram में देखिए।
ramp पर आप अपना scooter बिलकुल किसी भी height पर रोक सकते हैं। ये continuous range है। classical physics electron को ऐसे ही मानती थी: कोई भी orbit, कोई भी energy, एक smooth continuum।
staircase पर आप सिर्फ़ एक step पर खड़े हो सकते हैं। height एक, height दो, height तीन, और बीच में कभी आधा step नहीं। allowed positions अलग-अलग, गिनी जा सकने वाली हैं।
और Bohr की घोषणा बिलकुल यही है: atom एक staircase है, ramp नहीं। electron सिर्फ़ कुछ ख़ास orbits में रह सकता है, हर एक की अपनी तय energy के साथ, और उनके बीच कुछ भी नहीं।

यही एक idea दोनों classical failures को एक झटके में ख़त्म कर देता है। अगर electron सिर्फ़ तय steps पर बैठ सकता है, तो एक सबसे नीचला step है जिससे नीचे वो गिर नहीं सकता, यानी atom stable है। और energy सिर्फ़ steps के बीच तय jumps में निकल सकती है, इसीलिए colours तेज़ होते हैं।

तो postulate शब्द दिमाग़ में मज़बूती से रखिए। Bohr ने staircase मान लिया। उन्होंने साबित नहीं किया। और फ़िलहाल इतना काफ़ी है, क्योंकि आगे जो मायने रखता है वो ये कि कौन सी orbits allowed steps गिनी जाती हैं।

board_events.text: Which orbits are allowed?
Bohr's masterstroke was to quantise the angular momentum, not the energy directly.

board_events.text: An electron can sit only in an orbit where its angular momentum $mvr$ is a whole-number multiple of $h/2\pi$.
That integer $n$, the principal quantum number, is the step number on the staircase.
$n$ is the single knob that fixes the orbit size, the electron speed, and the atom's energy.
Crucially, an electron in one of these stationary states does NOT radiate, no matter what classical theory insists.

segments.text: So which orbits are the allowed steps? This is where Bohr's real genius shows, because the answer is not obvious and it is not what you might guess.
He did not quantise the energy directly. His masterstroke was to quantise the angular momentum, the quantity m v r, the electron's mass times its speed times its orbital radius.

The rule is this. An electron can only sit in an orbit where its angular momentum m v r is a whole-number multiple of h over two pi. Written out: m v r equals n h over two pi, where n is one, two, three, and so on.
Look carefully at what n is doing in the diagram. That integer n is called the principal quantum number, and it is quite literally the step number on the staircase. Step one, step two, step three.

And here is why this one idea is so powerful. n is a single knob. Turn it, and everything else in the atom follows. The size of the orbit, the speed of the electron, and the total energy of the atom are all fixed the moment you choose n.
We will derive all three of those in the next sections, and you will see them all fall out of this one quantisation rule. But hold the structure in mind now: one integer controls the entire atom.

There is one more piece of the postulate, and it is the part that directly repairs the stability failure. Bohr declared that an electron sitting in one of these allowed stationary states does not radiate. Full stop.

<whisper>It does not matter that classical theory insists an orbiting electron must radiate. Bohr simply overruled it. In a stationary state the electron holds its orbit and its energy indefinitely, and radiation happens only when it jumps between states. That is the whole trick, and it works.
तो कौन सी orbits allowed steps हैं? यहीं Bohr की असली प्रतिभा दिखती है, क्योंकि जवाब ज़ाहिर नहीं है और वो नहीं है जो आप शायद अंदाज़ा लगाएँ।
उन्होंने energy को सीधे quantise नहीं किया। उनका masterstroke था angular momentum को quantise करना — quantity m v r, यानी electron का mass गुणा speed गुणा orbital radius।
नियम ये है। electron सिर्फ़ उस orbit में बैठ सकता है जहाँ उसका angular momentum m v r, h over two pi का पूर्ण-संख्या गुणज हो। लिखिए: m v r बराबर n h over two pi, जहाँ n है एक, दो, तीन, वग़ैरह।
diagram में ध्यान से देखिए n क्या कर रहा है। वो integer n कहलाता है principal quantum number, और ये सचमुच staircase का step number है। step एक, step दो, step तीन।

और यही एक idea इतना ताक़तवर क्यों है, देखिए। n एक अकेला knob है। इसे घुमाइए, और atom में बाक़ी सब उसके पीछे चलता है। orbit का size, electron की speed, और atom की total energy — सब उसी पल तय हो जाते हैं जब आप n चुनते हैं।
अगले sections में हम तीनों derive करेंगे, और आप देखेंगे कि तीनों इसी एक quantisation rule से निकल आते हैं। पर structure अभी दिमाग़ में रखिए: एक integer पूरे atom को control करता है।
Postulate का एक हिस्सा और है, और यही वो हिस्सा है जो stability failure को सीधे ठीक करता है। Bohr ने घोषित किया कि इन allowed stationary states में बैठा electron radiate नहीं करता। बस।

<whisper>इससे फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ता कि classical theory कहती है orbiting electron को radiate करना ही चाहिए। Bohr ने उसे बस overrule कर दिया। stationary state में electron अपनी orbit और energy अनिश्चित काल तक रखता है, और radiation सिर्फ़ तब होता है जब वो states के बीच jump करे। यही पूरा trick है, और ये काम करता है।

board_events.text: Why only certain orbits survive
A decade later, de Broglie supplied the reason Bohr's quantisation is true.

board_events.text: The electron behaves like a wave. Only orbits whose circumference fits a whole number of electron wavelengths survive as steady standing waves.
Exactly like the fixed notes a tabla or a guitar string can sound: a non-fitting wave interferes with itself and cancels out.
Bohr's rule is not arbitrary after all. The staircase is really a set of resonant standing waves.

segments.text: Bohr's quantisation worked, but for a decade it sat there as an unexplained assumption. Why should angular momentum come in whole-number multiples of h over two pi? The answer, when it came, was gorgeous.
A decade later, Louis de Broglie supplied it. His idea was that the electron does not merely orbit like a tiny planet. It behaves like a wave, with a wavelength lambda equal to h over m v.

Now look at the two orbits in the diagram, and think about what a wave wrapped around a circle has to do to survive. On the left, the wave goes around and meets itself perfectly: a whole number of wavelengths fits the circumference. It reinforces itself into a steady standing wave.

On the right, the wave does not close. After one trip around, the crest arrives where a trough was. The wave interferes with itself and cancels out. That orbit simply cannot support a stable electron wave, so it is forbidden.

This is exactly like a musical instrument. A tabla or a guitar string can only sound certain fixed notes, the ones whose wavelengths fit the length of the string. Every other wavelength dies out. The atom is the same idea wrapped into a circle.
So the condition for an allowed orbit is that a whole number of wavelengths fits the circumference. Written down: two pi r n, the circumference, equals n times lambda.
Now substitute lambda equals h over m v and watch what happens. Two pi r n equals n times h over m v. Rearrange that, and you get m v r n equals n h over two pi.

<excited>That is exactly Bohr's quantisation rule, recovered for free. The postulate he had to assume by hand a decade earlier drops straight out of treating the electron as a standing wave. The staircase was never arbitrary. It is a set of resonant standing waves.
Bohr की quantisation काम करती थी, पर एक दशक तक वो एक बिना समझाई assumption की तरह पड़ी रही। angular momentum h over two pi के पूर्ण गुणजों में क्यों आए? जवाब जब आया, तो शानदार था।
एक दशक बाद Louis de Broglie ने वो जवाब दिया। उनका idea था कि electron सिर्फ़ एक नन्हे planet की तरह orbit नहीं करता। वो एक wave की तरह बर्ताव करता है, जिसकी wavelength lambda बराबर h over m v है।

अब diagram में दोनों orbits देखिए, और सोचिए कि एक circle के गिर्द लिपटी wave को बचने के लिए क्या करना पड़ता है। बाईं तरफ़, wave घूमकर ख़ुद से बिलकुल मिल जाती है: पूर्ण संख्या में wavelengths circumference में फ़िट होती हैं। वो ख़ुद को मज़बूत करके steady standing wave बन जाती है।
दाईं तरफ़, wave बंद नहीं होती। एक चक्कर के बाद crest वहाँ पहुँचता है जहाँ trough था। wave ख़ुद से interfere करके cancel हो जाती है। वो orbit stable electron wave नहीं रख सकती, तो forbidden है।

ये बिलकुल एक musical instrument जैसा है। तबला या guitar की string सिर्फ़ कुछ तय सुर बजा सकती है — वही जिनकी wavelengths string की लंबाई में फ़िट हों। बाक़ी हर wavelength मर जाती है। atom वही idea है, एक circle में लिपटा हुआ।
तो allowed orbit की शर्त यही है कि पूर्ण संख्या में wavelengths circumference में फ़िट हों। लिखिए: two pi r n, यानी circumference, बराबर n गुणा lambda।
अब lambda बराबर h over m v रखिए और देखिए क्या होता है। two pi r n बराबर n गुणा h over m v। इसे rearrange कीजिए, तो मिलता है m v r n बराबर n h over two pi।

<excited>यही बिलकुल Bohr की quantisation rule है, मुफ़्त में वापस मिल गई। जो postulate उन्हें एक दशक पहले हाथ से मानना पड़ा था, वो electron को standing wave मानने से सीधा निकल आता है। staircase कभी arbitrary थी ही नहीं। ये resonant standing waves का एक set है।

sections.subtopic: Bohr's Model and Energy Levels
sections.title: Where Bohr's model works, and where it breaks

board_events.text: The strict limits of a semiclassical model
The model applies ONLY to hydrogenic, one-electron systems: H, He+, Li2+, Be3+, and the like.

board_events.caption: One-electron systems against multi-electron atoms

board_events.text: It fails even for neutral helium, with just two electrons, because it ignores electron-electron repulsion.
It assumes a circular orbit and a point, infinitely heavy nucleus. Finite nuclear mass needs a small reduced-mass correction.
It is SEMICLASSICAL: a quantum rule grafted onto classical orbits.
It cannot explain the relative intensities of spectral lines, the fine splitting of lines, or the Zeeman effect.
It quantises only $n$. Real atoms need four quantum numbers; Bohr got the energies right by luck of hydrogen's pure Coulomb potential.

segments.text: Before we start calculating, we have to be honest about the boundaries of this model, because examiners test the boundaries just as hard as the formulas. Bohr's model is powerful, but it is fragile, and knowing where it snaps is real understanding.

The first and most important limit: it applies only to hydrogenic systems. That means one electron. Hydrogen itself, then singly ionised helium, doubly ionised lithium, triply ionised beryllium, and so on up the line. One electron, one nucleus.
Look at the two panels. On the left, a single electron in a clean Coulomb potential, and the model is exact. On the right, add even one more electron and it breaks.

This is a sharp trap, so hear it clearly: the model fails even for neutral helium, which has only two electrons. The reason is that the two electrons repel each other, and Bohr's model completely ignores electron-electron repulsion. Two electrons is already too many.

The second limit is geometric. The model assumes a perfectly circular orbit and a nucleus that is a point, and infinitely heavy. Both are idealisations. The finite mass of a real nucleus is handled by a small reduced-mass correction, which we will meet in the advanced worked example.

The third point is the deepest one. The model is semiclassical. It grafts a single quantum rule, the quantisation of angular momentum, onto otherwise classical orbits. It is a hybrid, and hybrids have limits.

Because it is only semiclassical, it cannot explain several things full quantum mechanics later did: the relative brightness of different spectral lines, the fine splitting of single lines into close pairs, or the way lines split in a magnetic field, the Zeeman effect.

<curious>And here is the subtle final point. Bohr quantises only one number, n. Real atoms need four quantum numbers to describe them. Bohr got the hydrogen energies right anyway, and the reason is almost embarrassing: for hydrogen's pure Coulomb potential, the energy happens to depend only on n. He got it right by the luck of the potential.

गणना शुरू करने से पहले हमें इस model की सीमाओं के बारे में ईमानदार होना पड़ेगा, क्योंकि examiners सीमाओं को formulas जितनी ही सख़्ती से जाँचते हैं। Bohr का model ताक़तवर है, पर नाज़ुक है, और ये जानना कि वो कहाँ टूटता है असली समझ है।

पहली और सबसे अहम सीमा: ये सिर्फ़ hydrogenic systems पर लागू होता है। यानी एक electron। ख़ुद hydrogen, फिर singly ionised helium, doubly ionised lithium, triply ionised beryllium, और इसी क्रम में आगे। एक electron, एक nucleus।
दोनों panels देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ एक clean Coulomb potential में अकेला electron, और model exact है। दाईं तरफ़ एक और electron जोड़िए और वो टूट जाता है।

ये एक तीखा trap है, तो साफ़ सुनिए: ये model neutral helium के लिए भी fail होता है, जिसमें सिर्फ़ दो electrons हैं। वजह ये कि दोनों electrons एक-दूसरे को repel करते हैं, और Bohr का model electron-electron repulsion को पूरी तरह नज़रअंदाज़ करता है। दो electrons ही बहुत ज़्यादा हैं।

दूसरी सीमा geometric है। model एक बिलकुल circular orbit और एक ऐसा nucleus मानता है जो एक point हो, और अनंत भारी। दोनों idealisations हैं। असली nucleus के finite mass को एक छोटे reduced-mass correction से संभाला जाता है, जो हम advanced worked example में देखेंगे।
तीसरी बात सबसे गहरी है। model semiclassical है। ये एक अकेला quantum rule, angular momentum की quantisation, वरना classical orbits पर चिपका देता है। ये एक hybrid है, और hybrids की सीमाएँ होती हैं।

चूँकि ये सिर्फ़ semiclassical है, ये कई चीज़ें नहीं समझा सकता जो आगे full quantum mechanics ने समझाईं: अलग-अलग spectral lines की चमक, एक line का पास-पास जोड़ियों में fine splitting, या magnetic field में lines का बँटना — Zeeman effect।

<curious>और यहाँ आख़िरी सूक्ष्म बात है। Bohr सिर्फ़ एक number, n, quantise करते हैं। असली atoms को describe करने के लिए चार quantum numbers चाहिए। Bohr फिर भी hydrogen की energies सही निकाल लेते हैं, और वजह लगभग शर्मिंदा करने वाली है: hydrogen के pure Coulomb potential के लिए energy सिर्फ़ n पर निर्भर होती है। उन्होंने इसे potential की क़िस्मत से सही पकड़ा।

sections.subtopic: Bohr's Model and Energy Levels
sections.title: Radius, speed, and energy: the three formulas

board_events.text: Everything for a hydrogenic atom, in three lines
For a nucleus of charge $+Ze$ and a single electron of mass $m$, the quantisation rule fixes three quantities.

board_events.latex: r_n \;=\; \frac{\varepsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{\pi m Z e^2} \;=\; a_0\,\frac{n^2}{Z}, \qquad a_0 = 0.529\ \text{\AA}

board_events.text: $a_0$ is the Bohr radius, the radius of the hydrogen ground orbit.
Radius scaling: $r_n \propto n^2/Z$. The orbit grows as $n^2$ and shrinks as $Z$ rises.
Scaling: $v_n \propto Z/n$. For hydrogen at $n = 1$, this is about $c/137$.
Scaling: $E_n \propto Z^2/n^2$. The negative sign means the electron is BOUND.

segments.text: Here is the whole quantitative payload of the subtopic, three formulas, one for each of the quantities that n controls. Learn these three and the scalings that ride on them, and most of the questions in this topic become routine.
First, the radius of the n-th orbit. r n equals epsilon nought n squared h squared, over pi m Z e squared. That is the full expression, but you almost never use it in that form.

Instead, collapse all the constants into one number. r n equals a nought times n squared over Z, where a nought is the Bohr radius, zero point five two nine angstroms. That a nought is the radius of the hydrogen ground orbit, and it is an anchor you must memorise.

Read the scaling straight off it: r n is proportional to n squared over Z. The orbit grows as n squared, so the n equals two orbit is four times the n equals one orbit, and it shrinks as Z rises, because a more highly charged nucleus pulls the electron in tighter.
Second, the orbital speed. v n equals Z e squared over two epsilon nought n h, which numerically is two point one nine times ten to the sixth, times Z over n, metres per second.

Its scaling is v n proportional to Z over n. Speed falls as you climb to higher orbits, and rises with nuclear charge. A striking anchor: for hydrogen at n equals one, the electron moves at about c over one hundred and thirty seven, roughly one percent of the speed of light.

Third, and most important, the total energy. E n equals minus m e to the fourth Z squared, over eight epsilon nought squared h squared n squared, which collapses to minus thirteen point six, times Z squared over n squared, electron volts.
The scaling is E n proportional to Z squared over n squared, and that thirteen point six electron volts is your third anchor. But do not skip past the minus sign. It is not decoration.

<whisper>The energy is negative because the electron is bound. A bound electron sits in an energy well, below the free-electron level of zero. The deeper the level, the more negative the number, and the harder it is to pull the electron out. That sign carries real physics, and dropping it will flip the meaning of every transition problem you solve.

यहाँ है इस subtopic का पूरा quantitative माल — तीन formulas, हर उस quantity के लिए एक जिसे n control करता है। इन तीन को और इन पर सवार scalings को याद कर लीजिए, और इस topic के ज़्यादातर सवाल routine हो जाते हैं।
पहला, n-th orbit का radius। r n बराबर epsilon nought n squared h squared, बटा pi m Z e squared। ये पूरा expression है, पर आप इसे इस रूप में लगभग कभी इस्तेमाल नहीं करते।

बजाय इसके, सारे constants को एक number में समेट लीजिए। r n बराबर a nought गुणा n squared over Z, जहाँ a nought है Bohr radius, zero point five two nine angstroms। वो a nought hydrogen के ground orbit का radius है, और एक anchor है जो आपको रटना है।

scaling सीधे पढ़िए: r n है n squared over Z के proportional। orbit n squared की तरह बढ़ता है, यानी n बराबर दो वाला orbit n बराबर एक से चार गुना है, और Z बढ़ने पर घटता है, क्योंकि ज़्यादा charged nucleus electron को कसकर अंदर खींचता है।
दूसरा, orbital speed। v n बराबर Z e squared over two epsilon nought n h, जो numerically है two point one nine times ten to the sixth, गुणा Z over n, metres per second।

इसका scaling है v n, Z over n के proportional। ऊँची orbits पर जाते ही speed घटती है, और nuclear charge के साथ बढ़ती है। एक चौंकाने वाला anchor: hydrogen में n बराबर एक पर electron करीब c over एक सौ सैंतीस से चलता है, यानी light की रफ़्तार का करीब एक percent।

तीसरा, और सबसे अहम, total energy। E n बराबर माइनस m e to the fourth Z squared, बटा eight epsilon nought squared h squared n squared, जो सिमटकर बनता है माइनस तेरह point छह, गुणा Z squared over n squared, electron volts।
scaling है E n, Z squared over n squared के proportional, और वो तेरह point छह electron volts आपका तीसरा anchor है। पर माइनस sign को छोड़कर मत निकलिए। वो सजावट नहीं है।

<whisper>energy negative है क्योंकि electron bound है। bound electron एक energy well में बैठा है, free-electron level zero से नीचे। level जितना गहरा, number उतना ज़्यादा negative, और electron को निकालना उतना ही मुश्किल। वो sign असली physics रखता है, और उसे छोड़ने से आपके हर transition problem का मतलब पलट जाएगा।

sections.subtopic: Bohr's Model and Energy Levels
sections.title: How the energy splits, and the motion of the orbit

board_events.text: The virial relations
The total energy is not the whole story. It splits into kinetic and potential parts in a fixed ratio.

board_events.caption: How the bound-state energy divides between kinetic and potential
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 800 328" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<line x1="360" y1="40" x2="360" y2="280" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<line x1="120" y1="160" x2="620" y2="160" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>

<rect x="200" y="160" width="350" height="45" fill="#2f7d5a"/>
<text x="196" y="272" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f7d5a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">KE = +13.6 Z²/n²</text>
<rect x="200" y="60" width="350" height="45" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#2f7d5a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<rect x="430" y="160" width="350" height="45" fill="#b3402f"/>
<text x="436" y="308" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">PE = 2Eₙ</text>
<rect x="430" y="118" width="350" height="45" fill="#c2820a"/>
<text x="530" y="140" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#c2820a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Eₙ = -13.6 Z²/n²</text>
<text x="30" y="30" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">HOW THE ENERGY SPLITS</text>
<text x="30" y="300" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">KE = minus E. PE = 2E = minus 2 KE. Freeing the electron costs exactly its kinetic energy.</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: The kinetic energy equals the magnitude of the total energy; the potential energy is twice the total, and negative.
$E = -\text{KE}$: freeing the electron to $E = 0$ costs exactly its kinetic energy. That is the ionisation energy.
Period grows steeply as $n^3$; frequency of revolution falls as $Z^2/n^3$.

segments.text: The total energy tells you how bound the electron is, but it hides a beautiful internal structure. That negative number is actually a sum of a positive kinetic energy and an even more negative potential energy, in a fixed ratio.

Look at the energy split in the diagram. The kinetic energy equals minus E n, which is plus thirteen point six Z squared over n squared electron volts. So the kinetic energy has exactly the same magnitude as the total energy, but the opposite sign.

The potential energy is twice the total energy, which is minus two times the kinetic energy. So if you know any one of these three numbers, you know all three. They are locked together by these virial relations.

The single most useful consequence is the relation E equals minus KE. Read what it says physically. To free the electron completely, you must lift it from its bound level all the way up to E equals zero.

And the size of that climb is exactly the kinetic energy the electron already has. So the energy needed to ionise the atom equals the electron's kinetic energy. For hydrogen's ground state that is thirteen point six electron volts, the ionisation energy, and now you see where that famous number comes from.
There are two more quantities the model gives you, describing the motion itself rather than the energy. The period of revolution T n is the circumference over the speed, two pi r n over v n.

Substitute the scalings and it comes out proportional to n cubed over Z squared. The period grows very steeply, as the cube of n. And the frequency of revolution, being one over the period, is proportional to Z squared over n cubed.

<curious>These period and frequency scalings look like minor footnotes, but J E E Advanced reaches for them constantly, often pairing the n cubed period growth with a transition question. Learn them now, because they are easy marks that most students never bother to memorise.

total energy बताती है electron कितना bound है, पर वो एक सुंदर अंदरूनी structure छुपाती है। वो negative number असल में एक positive kinetic energy और एक और भी negative potential energy का जोड़ है, एक तय ratio में।

diagram में energy split देखिए। kinetic energy बराबर माइनस E n, यानी plus तेरह point छह Z squared over n squared electron volts। तो kinetic energy का magnitude बिलकुल total energy जितना है, पर sign उलटा।
potential energy total energy की दोगुनी है, यानी माइनस दो गुणा kinetic energy। तो अगर आपको इन तीनों में से कोई एक number पता है, तीनों पता हैं। ये virial relations से आपस में बँधे हैं।
सबसे काम का नतीजा है relation E बराबर माइनस KE। इसका physical मतलब पढ़िए। electron को पूरी तरह आज़ाद करने के लिए आपको उसे उसके bound level से ऊपर E बराबर zero तक उठाना होगा।

और उस चढ़ाई का आकार बिलकुल वही kinetic energy है जो electron के पास पहले से है। तो atom को ionise करने की energy बराबर electron की kinetic energy। hydrogen के ground state के लिए वो तेरह point छह electron volts है, ionisation energy, और अब आपको दिखा वो मशहूर number कहाँ से आता है।
model आपको दो quantities और देता है, जो energy के बजाय ख़ुद गति describe करती हैं। revolution का period T n है circumference बटा speed, two pi r n over v n।

scalings रखिए तो वो निकलता है n cubed over Z squared के proportional। period बहुत तेज़ी से बढ़ता है, n के cube की तरह। और revolution की frequency, जो period की उलटी है, Z squared over n cubed के proportional है।

<curious>ये period और frequency वाले scalings छोटे footnotes लगते हैं, पर J E E Advanced इन्हें बार-बार इस्तेमाल करता है, अक्सर n cubed period growth को किसी transition सवाल के साथ जोड़कर। इन्हें अभी याद कर लीजिए, क्योंकि ये आसान marks हैं जिन्हें ज़्यादातर students रटने की ज़हमत नहीं उठाते।

board_events.text: Circular motion demands a net inward force. The only force present is the electrostatic attraction, so it must be exactly the centripetal force.
This is the classical half of the derivation. It contains no quantisation yet.
Equation (i) alone would allow any orbit. Quantisation, applied next, selects which ones are real.

segments.text: Now the derivation itself, the one that earns three to five marks on a board paper. It has five clean steps, and it combines exactly two physical ideas: one classical, one quantum. This section handles the classical half.

State the set-up first, every time. One electron of charge minus e and mass m moves in a circular orbit of radius r and speed v, around a stationary nucleus of charge plus Z e. That sentence frames the whole problem.

Step one is pure classical mechanics, and it is the force balance. Look at the diagram. Circular motion requires a net inward force, the centripetal force, or the electron would fly off in a straight line.

And here is the key observation: the only force present in this atom is the electrostatic attraction between the nucleus and the electron. There is nothing else. So that Coulomb attraction must be exactly what supplies the centripetal requirement.
Write that equality. One over four pi epsilon nought, times Z e times e, over r squared, the Coulomb force, equals m v squared over r, the centripetal force.
Now tidy it. Multiply both sides by r, and you get m v squared equals Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r. Label that equation one, because we lean on it twice more before we are done.

Notice carefully what equation one is, and what it is not. It is the entire classical content of the derivation, and it contains no quantisation whatsoever. Everything in it, Newton and Coulomb would have accepted without complaint.

<curious>And that is exactly why the model needs a second ingredient. Equation one, on its own, permits any orbit at all, any r you like, a smooth continuum, the very ramp that Bohr rejected. It is the quantisation rule, applied in the next section, that reaches in and selects which of those orbits are actually real.
अब derivation ख़ुद, वो जो board paper में तीन से पाँच marks दिलाती है। इसके पाँच साफ़ steps हैं, और ये ठीक दो physical ideas जोड़ती है: एक classical, एक quantum। ये section classical आधा संभालता है।

set-up पहले बताइए, हर बार। charge माइनस e और mass m वाला एक electron, radius r और speed v की circular orbit में, charge plus Z e के stationary nucleus के गिर्द घूमता है। यही वाक्य पूरे problem को ढाँचा देता है।
पहला step शुद्ध classical mechanics है, और वो है force balance। diagram देखिए। circular motion को एक net inward force चाहिए, centripetal force, वरना electron सीधी रेखा में उड़ जाएगा।

और यहाँ असली observation है: इस atom में मौजूद इकलौता force है nucleus और electron के बीच का electrostatic attraction। और कुछ नहीं। तो वही Coulomb attraction बिलकुल वही होना चाहिए जो centripetal ज़रूरत पूरी करे।
वो बराबरी लिखिए। one over four pi epsilon nought, गुणा Z e गुणा e, बटा r squared — Coulomb force — बराबर m v squared over r, centripetal force।
अब इसे साफ़ कीजिए। दोनों तरफ़ r से गुणा कीजिए, और मिलता है m v squared बराबर Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r। इसे equation एक कहिए, क्योंकि ख़त्म होने से पहले हम इस पर दो बार और टिकते हैं।
ध्यान से देखिए equation एक क्या है, और क्या नहीं। ये derivation का पूरा classical content है, और इसमें ज़रा भी quantisation नहीं। इसमें जो कुछ है, Newton और Coulomb बिना शिकायत मान लेते।

<curious>और इसीलिए model को एक दूसरी सामग्री चाहिए। equation एक अकेले किसी भी orbit को इजाज़त देता है, कोई भी r, एक smooth continuum, वही ramp जिसे Bohr ने ठुकराया। ये quantisation rule है, जो अगले section में लगती है, जो अंदर पहुँचकर चुनती है कि उन orbits में से कौन सी असल में real हैं।

board_events.text: Step two: from $mvr = nh/2\pi$, write $v = nh/2\pi mr$ and substitute into equation (i).

board_events.latex: m\left(\frac{nh}{2\pi mr}\right)^2 = \frac{Ze^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r} \;\Longrightarrow\; \frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m r^2} = \frac{Ze^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}

board_events.text: Step three: solve for the radius, giving $r_n = a_0\,n^2/Z$.
Step four: put $r_n$ back into the speed expression to get $v_n \propto Z/n$.
Total energy is negative and equals $-\text{KE}$: pulling the electron free costs exactly its kinetic energy.

segments.text: With the classical force balance in hand as equation one, the rest of the derivation is a cascade. Two physical inputs flow into three results, as the flowchart shows. Let me walk it.
Step two brings in the quantum ingredient. From Bohr's rule m v r equals n h over two pi, write v equals n h over two pi m r, and substitute it into equation one.
The left side becomes n squared h squared over four pi squared m r squared. Set that equal to the right side of equation one, Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r.

Step three is to solve that for r. The algebra tidies beautifully, and you get r n equals a nought times n squared over Z, with a nought equal to zero point five two nine angstroms. That is the radius formula, derived, not assumed.
And read off its meaning once more: the orbit grows as n squared, so the second orbit is four times the first, and it shrinks with Z, because a higher nuclear charge pulls the electron tighter.
Step four is quick. Take r n and put it back into the speed expression from the quantisation rule, and out comes v n proportional to Z over n. Radius done, speed done.

Step five assembles the energy. The kinetic energy, from equation one, is Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r. The potential energy is the Coulomb expression, minus Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r.

Add them: positive Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r plus minus Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r gives minus Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r. Substitute r n and you land on E n equals minus thirteen point six Z squared over n squared electron volts.

<whisper>And there is the clean result worth remembering: E equals minus KE. Adding a positive kinetic energy to a potential energy twice as large and negative leaves a total that is negative and exactly the size of the kinetic energy. Pulling the electron free to zero costs precisely its kinetic energy, and that is the ionisation energy.
classical force balance को equation एक के रूप में हाथ में लेकर, बाक़ी derivation एक cascade है। दो physical inputs तीन results में बहते हैं, जैसा flowchart दिखाता है। चलिए इसे चलते हैं।
दूसरा step quantum सामग्री लाता है। Bohr के rule m v r बराबर n h over two pi से v बराबर n h over two pi m r लिखिए, और equation एक में रखिए।
बाईं तरफ़ बनती है n squared h squared over four pi squared m r squared। इसे equation एक की दाईं तरफ़, Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r, के बराबर रखिए।

तीसरा step है इसे r के लिए हल करना। algebra ख़ूबसूरती से सिमटता है, और मिलता है r n बराबर a nought गुणा n squared over Z, जहाँ a nought बराबर zero point five two nine angstroms। यही radius formula है, derive किया गया, माना नहीं।
और इसका मतलब एक बार फिर पढ़िए: orbit n squared की तरह बढ़ता है, यानी दूसरा orbit पहले से चार गुना, और Z के साथ घटता है, क्योंकि ऊँचा nuclear charge electron को कसकर खींचता है।
चौथा step तेज़ है। r n लीजिए और quantisation rule वाली speed expression में वापस रखिए, और निकलता है v n, Z over n के proportional। radius हुआ, speed हुआ।
पाँचवाँ step energy जोड़ता है। kinetic energy, equation एक से, है Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r। potential energy है Coulomb expression, माइनस Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r।

इन्हें जोड़िए: positive Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r जमा माइनस Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought r बराबर माइनस Z e squared over eight pi epsilon nought r। r n रखिए और मिलता है E n बराबर माइनस तेरह point छह Z squared over n squared electron volts।

<whisper>और यहाँ है याद रखने लायक़ साफ़ नतीजा: E बराबर माइनस KE। एक positive kinetic energy को उससे दोगुनी बड़ी और negative potential energy में जोड़ने पर बचता है एक total जो negative है और बिलकुल kinetic energy जितना। electron को zero तक आज़ाद करना ठीक उसकी kinetic energy माँगता है, और यही ionisation energy है।

board_events.text: Treat the electron as a standing wave around the orbit. Stability requires a whole number of wavelengths to fit the circumference.
This is Bohr's quantisation rule, now EXPLAINED rather than merely assumed.
The same result seen in the concept section, now written as a formal two-line derivation for the exam.

segments.text: We met this idea in the concept section, but it also appears as a short formal derivation on papers, so let us write it out cleanly, in two lines, the way an examiner wants to see it.
The goal is to justify Bohr's postulate. Bohr simply assumed that m v r equals n h over two pi. de Broglie showed why that must be true, starting from the electron being a wave.

Treat the electron as a standing wave wrapped around its orbit. Look again at the figure: for the wave to be stable, it must meet itself smoothly after one loop, which requires a whole number of wavelengths to fit the circumference.
Write that condition. The circumference two pi r n equals n times lambda, the wavelength, for integer n. That is the standing-wave requirement, and it is the whole physical input.
Now bring in de Broglie's relation for the wavelength: lambda equals h over m v. Substitute it into the standing-wave condition, so two pi r n equals n times h over m v.
Rearrange, moving the m v across, and you get m v r n equals n h over two pi. That is Bohr's quantisation rule exactly, no longer assumed but now explained.
This is a very high-value derivation to have ready, because it is short, it is clean, and it connects two chapters, wave nature of matter and the Bohr model, in a way examiners love to reward.

<excited>And step back to appreciate what just happened conceptually. Bohr's boldest, most arbitrary-looking assumption, the one he wrote down by hand with no justification, turns out to be nothing more than the condition for a standing wave to fit around a loop. The atom is a resonating instrument, and n is which harmonic it is playing.
ये idea हम concept section में मिले थे, पर ये papers पर एक छोटी formal derivation के रूप में भी आता है, तो चलिए इसे साफ़ लिखते हैं, दो लाइनों में, जैसे examiner देखना चाहता है।
मक़सद है Bohr के postulate को justify करना। Bohr ने बस मान लिया कि m v r बराबर n h over two pi। de Broglie ने दिखाया वो क्यों सच होना चाहिए, electron के wave होने से शुरू करके।

electron को उसकी orbit के गिर्द लिपटी standing wave मानिए। figure फिर देखिए: wave के stable होने के लिए उसे एक loop के बाद ख़ुद से smoothly मिलना होगा, जिसके लिए पूर्ण संख्या में wavelengths circumference में फ़िट होनी चाहिए।
वो शर्त लिखिए। circumference two pi r n बराबर n गुणा lambda, wavelength, पूर्णांक n के लिए। यही standing-wave requirement है, और यही पूरा physical input है।
अब de Broglie का wavelength वाला relation लाइए: lambda बराबर h over m v। इसे standing-wave condition में रखिए, तो two pi r n बराबर n गुणा h over m v।
rearrange कीजिए, m v को दूसरी तरफ़ ले जाकर, और मिलता है m v r n बराबर n h over two pi। यही बिलकुल Bohr की quantisation rule है, अब मानी हुई नहीं बल्कि समझाई हुई।
ये तैयार रखने लायक़ बहुत high-value derivation है, क्योंकि छोटी है, साफ़ है, और दो chapters — matter की wave nature और Bohr model — को इस तरह जोड़ती है जिसे examiners इनाम देना पसंद करते हैं।

<excited>और conceptually जो अभी हुआ उसकी क़दर कीजिए। Bohr की सबसे बोल्ड, सबसे arbitrary दिखने वाली assumption, जो उन्होंने बिना justification हाथ से लिखी थी, निकली महज़ एक loop के गिर्द standing wave के फ़िट होने की शर्त। atom एक बजता हुआ instrument है, और n बताता है वो कौन सा harmonic बजा रहा है।

board_events.text: Radius first. Use $r_n = a_0\,n^2/Z$ with $a_0 = 0.529$ \AA, $Z = 1$, $n = 3$.
Energy next. Use $E_n = -13.6\,Z^2/n^2$ with $Z = 1$, $n = 3$.
Both drop straight out of the scalings. No full expression needed - this is a one-minute question.

segments.text: Let us start applying these formulas with the most direct board-level question there is. For a hydrogen atom, find the radius and the energy of the n equals three orbit. Two quantities, one orbit.
The first thing to register is the species: hydrogen, so Z equals one. That keeps everything simple, but train yourself to check Z first, always, because the next examples will not be so kind.

For the radius, reach for the scaling form, not the full expression. r n equals a nought times n squared over Z. Put in a nought equal to zero point five two nine angstroms, Z equal to one, and n equal to three.

n squared is nine, Z is one, so r three equals zero point five two nine times nine, which is four point seven six angstroms. In metres that is four point seven six times ten to the minus ten. The third orbit is nine times the size of the ground orbit, exactly as n squared demands.
For the energy, use the energy scaling. E n equals minus thirteen point six times Z squared over n squared. Z squared is one, n squared is nine.
So E three equals minus thirteen point six over nine, which is minus one point five one electron volts. Note the sign carried through: it is negative, because the electron is bound.
And that is the entire question. Both answers dropped straight out of the scalings, with no need to touch the full expressions with all their epsilon noughts and h squareds.

<curious>That is the habit I want you building from the very first example. For hydrogenic questions, the scaling forms plus the three anchors are almost always all you need. This should be a one-minute question in the exam, leaving your time for the ones that actually fight back.
इन formulas को लगाना सबसे सीधे board-level सवाल से शुरू करते हैं। hydrogen atom के लिए, n बराबर तीन orbit का radius और energy निकालिए। दो quantities, एक orbit।
पहली बात जो दर्ज करनी है वो है species: hydrogen, यानी Z बराबर एक। इससे सब आसान रहता है, पर ख़ुद को Z पहले check करने की आदत डालिए, हमेशा, क्योंकि अगले examples इतने दयालु नहीं होंगे।
radius के लिए scaling form पकड़िए, पूरा expression नहीं। r n बराबर a nought गुणा n squared over Z। रखिए a nought बराबर zero point five two nine angstroms, Z बराबर एक, और n बराबर तीन।

n squared है नौ, Z है एक, तो r तीन बराबर zero point five two nine गुणा नौ, यानी four point seven six angstroms। metres में वो four point seven six times ten to the minus ten है। तीसरा orbit ground orbit से नौ गुना बड़ा है, बिलकुल जैसा n squared माँगता है।
energy के लिए energy scaling इस्तेमाल कीजिए। E n बराबर माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा Z squared over n squared। Z squared है एक, n squared है नौ।
तो E तीन बराबर माइनस तेरह point छह बटा नौ, यानी माइनस one point five one electron volts। sign साथ ले जाने पर ध्यान दीजिए: ये negative है, क्योंकि electron bound है।
और यही पूरा सवाल है। दोनों जवाब सीधे scalings से निकल आए, बिना उन पूरे expressions को छुए जिनमें epsilon noughts और h squared भरे हैं।

<curious>यही आदत मैं चाहता हूँ आप पहले ही example से बनाएँ। hydrogenic सवालों के लिए scaling forms और तीन anchors लगभग हमेशा काफ़ी होते हैं। ये exam में एक-मिनट का सवाल होना चाहिए, ताकि आपका वक़्त उन सवालों के लिए बचे जो सचमुच लड़ते हैं।

board_events.text: Since $E_n \propto Z^2/n^2$, the energy equals $-13.6$ eV exactly when $Z^2/n^2 = 1$, that is, whenever $Z = n$.

segments.text: This next one is a beautiful N E E T trap, and it rewards spotting a pattern instead of grinding through arithmetic. Which of three species has the same energy as ground-state hydrogen, minus thirteen point six electron volts?
The options are singly ionised helium in n equals two, doubly ionised lithium in n equals three, and triply ionised beryllium in n equals two. Three hydrogenic ions, each in a specified orbit.

The trap has two teeth. First, students who forget the Z squared and treat these like hydrogen. Second, and this catches even careful students, those who compute one match, feel satisfied, and stop, when the question may have several correct answers.

So find the pattern instead of computing three times. The energy is minus thirteen point six times Z squared over n squared. It equals minus thirteen point six exactly when Z squared over n squared equals one, which happens whenever Z equals n. That is the whole shortcut: check whether Z equals n.
Look at the three panels with that test in hand. Helium plus: Z is two, n is two, so Z equals n. It matches, minus thirteen point six times four over four is minus thirteen point six. Tick.
Lithium two plus: Z is three, n is three, so Z equals n again. It also matches, minus thirteen point six times nine over nine is minus thirteen point six. Tick.
Beryllium three plus: Z is four, n is two, so Z does not equal n. It fails. Minus thirteen point six times sixteen over four is minus fifty four point four electron volts, nowhere near the target.

<whisper>So the answer is both one and two, and that is the trap sprung. A student who computes helium, sees the match, and moves on has thrown away half the marks. The Z equals n trick does the whole problem in your head, and, crucially, it makes you check all three instead of stopping at the first hit.
अगला एक सुंदर N E E T trap है, और ये arithmetic पीसने के बजाय pattern पहचानने का इनाम देता है। तीन species में से किसकी energy ground-state hydrogen जितनी है, माइनस तेरह point छह electron volts?
options हैं singly ionised helium n बराबर दो में, doubly ionised lithium n बराबर तीन में, और triply ionised beryllium n बराबर दो में। तीन hydrogenic ions, हर एक अपनी बताई orbit में।

trap के दो दाँत हैं। पहला, जो students Z squared भूलकर इन्हें hydrogen मान लेते हैं। दूसरा, और ये सावधान students को भी पकड़ता है, वो जो एक match निकालकर, संतुष्ट होकर रुक जाते हैं, जबकि सवाल के कई सही जवाब हो सकते हैं।

तो तीन बार गिनने के बजाय pattern ढूँढिए। energy है माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा Z squared over n squared। ये बिलकुल माइनस तेरह point छह तब होती है जब Z squared over n squared बराबर एक, जो तब होता है जब Z बराबर n। यही पूरा शॉर्टकट है: देखिए Z बराबर n है या नहीं।
उस test के साथ तीनों panels देखिए। helium plus: Z है दो, n है दो, यानी Z बराबर n। match करता है, माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा चार बटा चार बराबर माइनस तेरह point छह। सही।
lithium two plus: Z है तीन, n है तीन, यानी फिर Z बराबर n। ये भी match करता है, माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा नौ बटा नौ बराबर माइनस तेरह point छह। सही।
beryllium three plus: Z है चार, n है दो, यानी Z बराबर n नहीं। ये fail होता है। माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा सोलह बटा चार बराबर माइनस चौवन point चार electron volts, target के आसपास भी नहीं।

<whisper>तो जवाब है एक और दो दोनों, और यहीं trap फँस गया। जो student helium गिनकर, match देखकर आगे बढ़ गया उसने आधे marks फेंक दिए। Z बराबर n वाला trick पूरा problem दिमाग़ में कर देता है, और सबसे अहम, ये आपसे तीनों जँचवा देता है, पहले hit पर रुकने नहीं देता।

board_events.text: Step one, the orbital speed: $v_2 = 2.19\times10^{6}\times Z/n = 2.19\times10^{6}\times 1/2 = 1.095\times10^{6}$ m s$^{-1}$.
Step three, check $2\pi r_2 = n\lambda$. With $r_2 = 0.529\times 4 = 2.12$ \AA:
Exactly two wavelengths fit the n = 2 orbit. The wave picture and the quantisation rule agree.

segments.text: This J E E Main question makes the standing-wave idea concrete by turning it into a calculation. Find the de Broglie wavelength of the electron in the n equals two orbit of hydrogen, and then verify that it satisfies Bohr's standing-wave condition.

The picture is the whole point: for n equals two, exactly two full wavelengths should fit around the orbit. We are going to compute the wavelength, compute the circumference, and check that the circumference is two wavelengths. If Bohr is right, it must be.

Step one, get the orbital speed. Use the speed anchor: v n equals two point one nine times ten to the sixth, times Z over n. With Z equal to one and n equal to two, that is half of two point one nine times ten to the sixth, so one point zero nine five times ten to the sixth metres per second.

Step two, the de Broglie wavelength. Lambda equals h over m v. Put h equal to six point six three times ten to the minus thirty four, the electron mass nine point one times ten to the minus thirty one, and the speed we just found.
Work it through and lambda comes out at about six point six six times ten to the minus ten metres, which is six point six six angstroms. That is the wavelength of the electron wave in this orbit.

Step three is the verification, and this is where it becomes satisfying. Compute the circumference. The radius r two is a nought times four, which is zero point five two nine times four, or two point one two angstroms.

So the circumference two pi r two is two pi times two point one two, which is thirteen point three angstroms. Now compare that to the wavelength: thirteen point three is exactly two times six point six six. The circumference is two wavelengths, precisely.

<excited>And that is the standing-wave condition confirmed by direct calculation. For the n equals two orbit, two whole wavelengths fit the circumference, no more and no less. The wave picture and Bohr's quantisation rule are not two different ideas that happen to agree. They are the same idea, and this numerical check proves it.

ये J E E Main सवाल standing-wave idea को एक गणना में बदलकर ठोस बना देता है। hydrogen के n बराबर दो orbit में electron की de Broglie wavelength निकालिए, फिर verify कीजिए कि वो Bohr की standing-wave condition मानती है।

तस्वीर ही पूरी बात है: n बराबर दो के लिए, orbit के गिर्द ठीक दो पूरी wavelengths फ़िट होनी चाहिए। हम wavelength निकालेंगे, circumference निकालेंगे, और जाँचेंगे कि circumference दो wavelengths है। अगर Bohr सही हैं, तो होना ही चाहिए।

पहला step, orbital speed निकालिए। speed anchor इस्तेमाल कीजिए: v n बराबर two point one nine times ten to the sixth, गुणा Z over n। Z बराबर एक और n बराबर दो के साथ, वो two point one nine times ten to the sixth का आधा है, यानी one point zero nine five times ten to the sixth metres per second।

दूसरा step, de Broglie wavelength। lambda बराबर h over m v। रखिए h बराबर six point six three times ten to the minus thirty four, electron mass nine point one times ten to the minus thirty one, और अभी निकाली speed।
इसे चलाइए और lambda निकलती है करीब six point six six times ten to the minus ten metres, यानी six point six six angstroms। यही इस orbit में electron wave की wavelength है।
तीसरा step है verification, और यहीं ये संतोषजनक बनता है। circumference निकालिए। radius r दो है a nought गुणा चार, यानी zero point five two nine गुणा चार, या two point one two angstroms।

तो circumference two pi r दो है two pi गुणा two point one two, यानी thirteen point three angstroms। अब इसकी तुलना wavelength से कीजिए: thirteen point three बिलकुल two गुणा six point six six है। circumference दो wavelengths है, ठीक-ठीक।

<excited>और यही standing-wave condition, सीधी गणना से पुष्ट। n बराबर दो orbit के लिए दो पूरी wavelengths circumference में फ़िट होती हैं, न ज़्यादा न कम। wave picture और Bohr की quantisation rule दो अलग ideas नहीं जो संयोग से मिल जाती हैं। ये एक ही idea हैं, और ये numerical check इसे साबित करता है।

board_events.text: JEE Advanced: swapping the electron for a muon

A negative muon, $m_\mu = 207\,m_e$, is captured by a proton to form muonic hydrogen. Estimate the ground-state radius and energy, then refine the energy with the reduced mass, given $m_p = 1836\,m_e$.

board_events.caption: The naive estimate and the reduced-mass correction
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 720 340" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="24" y="28" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">MUONIC HYDROGEN: swap the electron for a muon, 207 times heavier</text>
<circle cx="150" cy="170" r="16" fill="#b3402f"/>
<text x="134" y="175" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">p</text>
<circle cx="150" cy="170" r="40" fill="none" stroke="#2b6ca3" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<circle cx="190" cy="170" r="7" fill="#2b6ca3"/>
<text x="120" y="234" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#2b6ca3" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">tiny muon orbit</text>
<text x="200" y="130" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">r ~ 1/m, so 207x smaller</text>
<rect x="350" y="56" width="340" height="120" rx="8" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.5"/>

<text x="366" y="116" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">r = 0.529 A / 207 = 2.56 e-13 m</text>
<text x="366" y="146" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#c2820a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">E = -13.6 times 207 = -2.82 keV</text>

<text x="366" y="222" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f7d5a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Reduced mass mu = 186 me:</text>
<text x="366" y="252" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f7d5a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">E = -13.6 times 186 = -2.53 keV</text>
<text x="366" y="284" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">a 10% reduction; proton radius ~1 fm,</text>
<text x="366" y="302" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">so point-nucleus still holds at 256 fm</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Key idea: all Bohr formulas were derived with the electron mass $m$. Replace $m$ by the orbiting particle's mass. Since $r \propto 1/m$ and $E \propto m$.
A 10% reduction from the naive value. And $r \approx 256$ fm, vastly larger than the proton's $\sim 1$ fm, so the point-nucleus assumption still holds.

segments.text: Now a genuinely advanced problem, testing whether you understand where the electron mass enters Bohr's formulas. A negative muon, two hundred and seven times heavier than an electron, is captured by a proton to form muonic hydrogen. Find the ground-state radius and energy, first naively, then corrected.

The key idea unlocks the whole thing. Every Bohr formula was derived using the electron mass m. Nothing in the derivation actually required the orbiting particle to be an electron. So for a muon, you simply replace m by the muon mass everywhere.

Trace the mass dependence. The radius goes as one over m, so a heavier particle sits in a smaller orbit. The energy goes as m, so it sits in a deeper level. A muon, two hundred and seven times heavier, does both dramatically.

Part a, the naive estimate, treating the proton as infinitely heavy. The radius is the Bohr radius divided by two hundred and seven, which is about two point five six times ten to the minus thirteen metres. The muon orbits two hundred and seven times closer in than an electron would.

And the energy is minus thirteen point six times two hundred and seven, which is about minus two point eight two kilo electron volts. Two hundred and seven times deeper than hydrogen's ground state. Muonic atoms are tightly, tightly bound.

Part b refines the energy using the reduced mass, because two hundred and seven times the electron mass is no longer negligible against the proton. The reduced mass mu is m mu times m p over their sum, which works out to about one hundred and eighty six electron masses.

Since the energy scales with the orbiting mass, use mu in place of the bare muon mass. E one is minus thirteen point six times one hundred and eighty six, about minus two point five three kilo electron volts, a ten percent reduction. For ordinary hydrogen the same correction is only zero point zero five percent, so this is a rare case where reduced mass matters.

<curious>And finish with the sanity check the examiner is really testing. The muon orbits at about two hundred and fifty six femtometres, while the proton is only about one femtometre across. So even for this tiny orbit the muon stays vastly outside the nucleus, and the point-nucleus assumption holds. For muonic heavy atoms it would not, a lovely link back to the nuclear-size theme of Part one.

अब एक सचमुच advanced problem, जो जाँचता है कि Bohr के formulas में electron mass कहाँ घुसता है। एक negative muon, electron से दो सौ सात गुना भारी, एक proton द्वारा पकड़ा जाकर muonic hydrogen बनाता है। ground-state radius और energy निकालिए, पहले naively, फिर corrected।

key idea पूरी चीज़ खोल देता है। हर Bohr formula electron mass m से derive हुआ था। derivation में असल में कहीं ज़रूरी नहीं था कि orbiting particle electron ही हो। तो muon के लिए, आप बस हर जगह m को muon mass से बदल देते हैं।

mass dependence पर नज़र रखिए। radius चलता है one over m की तरह, तो भारी particle छोटी orbit में बैठता है। energy चलती है m की तरह, तो गहरे level में। muon, दो सौ सात गुना भारी, दोनों नाटकीय ढंग से करता है।

भाग a, naive estimate, proton को अनंत भारी मानकर। radius है Bohr radius बटा दो सौ सात, यानी करीब two point five six times ten to the minus thirteen metres। muon electron से दो सौ सात गुना अंदर orbit करता है।
और energy है माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा दो सौ सात, यानी करीब माइनस two point eight two kilo electron volts। hydrogen के ground state से दो सौ सात गुना गहरी। muonic atoms बहुत, बहुत कसकर bound हैं।

भाग b energy को reduced mass से refine करता है, क्योंकि electron mass का दो सौ सात गुना अब proton के सामने नज़रअंदाज़ करने लायक़ नहीं। reduced mass mu है m mu गुणा m p बटा उनका जोड़, जो निकलता है करीब एक सौ छियासी electron masses।

चूँकि energy orbiting mass के साथ चलती है, muon mass की जगह mu इस्तेमाल कीजिए। E एक है माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा एक सौ छियासी, करीब माइनस two point five three kilo electron volts, दस percent की कमी। सामान्य hydrogen के लिए वही correction सिर्फ़ zero point zero five percent है, तो ये दुर्लभ मामला है जहाँ reduced mass मायने रखता है।

<curious>और उस sanity check के साथ ख़त्म कीजिए जो examiner असल में जाँच रहा है। muon करीब दो सौ छप्पन femtometres पर orbit करता है, जबकि proton सिर्फ़ करीब एक femtometre चौड़ा है। तो इस नन्ही orbit के लिए भी muon nucleus से बहुत बाहर रहता है, और point-nucleus assumption टिकता है। muonic भारी atoms के लिए ये नहीं टिकता, जो Part एक के nuclear-size theme से एक प्यारा जोड़ है।

board_events.text: Pitfall 1: dropping the Z for ions

board_events.caption: Why the Z powers cannot be dropped
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 720 320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="24" y="28" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">THE SINGLE MOST COMMON ERROR: DROPPING Z</text>
<rect x="40" y="60" width="300" height="200" rx="8" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="60" y="92" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Carry the Z powers:</text>
<text x="60" y="130" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#c2820a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Energy  ~  Z squared</text>
<text x="60" y="164" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#2f7d5a" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Radius  ~  1 / Z</text>
<text x="60" y="198" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#2b6ca3" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Speed  ~  Z</text>
<text x="60" y="236" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Check the species FIRST.</text>
<rect x="370" y="60" width="310" height="200" rx="8" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#b3402f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="390" y="92" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Treating an ion as hydrogen:</text>
<text x="390" y="130" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">He+ ground state is NOT -13.6</text>
<text x="390" y="156" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">it is -13.6 times 4 = -54.4 eV</text>
<text x="390" y="196" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Forgetting Z squared here loses</text>
<text x="390" y="216" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">the whole question.</text>
<text x="30" y="300" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">Always ask: is this hydrogen, or a hydrogenic ion?</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: The formulas carry $Z^2$ for energy, $1/Z$ for radius, and $Z$ for speed.
Treating He+ or Li2+ like hydrogen is the single most common error in this topic.
Always check first: is the species hydrogen, or a hydrogenic ion? He+ ground state is $-54.4$ eV, not $-13.6$ eV.
Pitfall 2: sign and split confusion
Mixing these up flips signs in every transition and ionisation problem you attempt.

segments.text: Two pitfalls to start, and the first is, without competition, the most common mistake in this entire topic. It costs more marks than everything else here combined.

Pitfall one is dropping the Z when the species is an ion. The formulas carry the nuclear charge in specific powers: Z squared for the energy, one over Z for the radius, and Z to the first power for the speed. Look at the panel and fix those powers.

The error is treating a hydrogenic ion as though it were hydrogen. Ask for the ground-state energy of singly ionised helium, and a student writes minus thirteen point six electron volts on autopilot. It is wrong.

Helium plus has Z equal to two, so the energy carries a factor of Z squared, which is four. The ground state is minus thirteen point six times four, which is minus fifty four point four electron volts. Forgetting that factor of four does not lose you a little accuracy, it loses you the whole question.
So build one reflex above all others in this topic: before you write any number, check the species. Is this hydrogen, or a hydrogenic ion? Get the Z right, and the rest is arithmetic.

Pitfall two is sign and split confusion, and it is quieter but just as damaging. The total energy E n is negative. The kinetic energy is positive, equal to the magnitude of E n. And the potential energy is twice the total energy, which is minus two times the kinetic energy.

Those signs are not bookkeeping, they carry physics. The kinetic energy has to be positive, it is a speed squared. The potential energy has to be the most negative of the three, it is the deep Coulomb well the electron sits in.

<whisper>And here is where it bites. Every transition problem and every ionisation problem is a subtraction of two of these energies. If you flip a single sign, you flip the direction of the transition, and an emission becomes an absorption. Get the signs anchored now: E negative, KE positive and equal in size, PE twice E and negative.
शुरू में दो pitfalls, और पहली, बिना किसी मुक़ाबले, इस पूरे topic की सबसे आम ग़लती है। ये यहाँ बाक़ी सबसे मिलाकर भी ज़्यादा marks काटती है।

पहली pitfall है ion होने पर Z छोड़ देना। formulas nuclear charge को ख़ास powers में रखते हैं: energy के लिए Z squared, radius के लिए one over Z, और speed के लिए Z की पहली power। panel देखिए और वो powers बिठा लीजिए।
ग़लती है एक hydrogenic ion को ऐसे मानना जैसे वो hydrogen हो। singly ionised helium की ground-state energy पूछिए, और student autopilot पर माइनस तेरह point छह electron volts लिख देता है। ग़लत है।

helium plus का Z बराबर दो है, तो energy में Z squared का factor है, यानी चार। ground state है माइनस तेरह point छह गुणा चार, यानी माइनस चौवन point चार electron volts। वो चार का factor भूलना थोड़ी accuracy नहीं, पूरा सवाल खो देता है।
तो इस topic में सबसे ऊपर एक reflex बनाइए: कोई number लिखने से पहले species check कीजिए। ये hydrogen है, या hydrogenic ion? Z सही कीजिए, बाक़ी बस arithmetic है।

दूसरी pitfall है sign और split confusion, और ये चुपचाप है पर उतनी ही नुक़सानदेह। total energy E n negative है। kinetic energy positive है, E n के magnitude जितनी। और potential energy total energy की दोगुनी है, यानी माइनस दो गुणा kinetic energy।

वो signs हिसाब-किताब नहीं, physics रखते हैं। kinetic energy को positive होना ही है, वो speed squared है। potential energy को तीनों में सबसे negative होना है, वो गहरा Coulomb well है जिसमें electron बैठा है।

<whisper>और यहीं ये काटती है। हर transition problem और हर ionisation problem इन में से दो energies का घटाव है। एक sign पलटाइए, transition की दिशा पलट जाती है, और emission बन जाता है absorption। signs अभी बिठा लीजिए: E negative, KE positive और बराबर आकार, PE दोगुनी E और negative।

board_events.text: Pitfall 3: postulate versus consequence

board_events.caption: What is assumed against what is derived

board_events.text: Angular momentum is POSTULATED quantised. Energy, radius, and speed quantisation all FOLLOW from it.
Exam MCQs test exactly this distinction. Picking 'energy' as the postulate confuses a result with the foundation.
Pitfall 4: over-extending Bohr
The model is valid ONLY for one-electron, hydrogenic systems.
Applying it to neutral helium or sodium earns zero marks, however clean your arithmetic looks.
The moment a system has two or more electrons, Bohr is the wrong tool. Reach for it only when there is a single electron.

segments.text: The last two pitfalls are conceptual rather than numerical, and both are favourite discriminators on multiple-choice papers, the kind of question designed to separate understanding from memorisation.

Pitfall three is confusing the postulate with its consequences. Look at the diagram. At the top sits the one thing Bohr actually postulated: that the angular momentum m v r is quantised. Everything below it, the quantisation of energy, of radius, of speed, is derived from that single assumption.

So when an MCQ asks what Bohr's second postulate quantises, the answer is angular momentum, and only angular momentum. Energy, radius, and speed are all quantised too, but as consequences, not as the postulate.

Students who pick energy are not exactly wrong that energy is quantised, they are wrong about what is foundational versus what is derived. That is precisely the distinction the examiner built the question to test, so hold it firmly.
Pitfall four is over-extending the model past its one-electron limit, and it is worth being blunt about the penalty. The Bohr model is valid only for hydrogenic, single-electron systems.

Apply it to neutral helium, with two electrons, or to sodium, with eleven, and you earn zero marks, no matter how clean and confident your arithmetic looks. Neat working on an invalid model is still worth nothing.
The rule is sharp and easy to apply: the moment a system has two or more electrons, Bohr is the wrong tool, because it ignores the electron-electron repulsion that then dominates.

<curious>So make the check automatic. Before you deploy any Bohr formula, count the electrons. One electron, and the whole toolkit is yours. Two or more, and you must put it down, however tempting the clean scalings look. Knowing when not to use a tool is as much a part of the answer as using it well.
आख़िरी दो pitfalls numerical के बजाय conceptual हैं, और दोनों multiple-choice papers के पसंदीदा discriminators हैं — वो सवाल जो समझ को रटने से अलग करने के लिए बने होते हैं।

तीसरी pitfall है postulate को उसके consequences से गड्डमड्ड करना। diagram देखिए। ऊपर बैठी है वो एक चीज़ जो Bohr ने सचमुच postulate की: कि angular momentum m v r quantised है। उसके नीचे सब कुछ — energy, radius, speed की quantisation — उसी एक assumption से derive होता है।

तो जब कोई MCQ पूछे कि Bohr का दूसरा postulate क्या quantise करता है, जवाब है angular momentum, और सिर्फ़ angular momentum। energy, radius, speed भी quantised हैं, पर consequences के रूप में, postulate के रूप में नहीं।

जो students energy चुनते हैं वो बिलकुल ग़लत नहीं कि energy quantised है, वो इस बारे में ग़लत हैं कि foundational क्या है और derived क्या। examiner ने सवाल ठीक यही फ़र्क़ जाँचने को बनाया है, तो इसे मज़बूती से पकड़िए।
चौथी pitfall है model को उसकी one-electron सीमा के पार खींचना, और सज़ा के बारे में साफ़ रहना ज़रूरी है। Bohr model सिर्फ़ hydrogenic, single-electron systems के लिए valid है।

इसे neutral helium पर, जिसमें दो electrons हैं, या sodium पर, जिसमें ग्यारह, लगाइए और आपको शून्य marks मिलते हैं, चाहे आपकी arithmetic कितनी साफ़ और आत्मविश्वासी दिखे। invalid model पर सुथरी working की भी क़ीमत शून्य है।
नियम तीखा और लगाने में आसान है: जिस पल किसी system में दो या ज़्यादा electrons हों, Bohr ग़लत tool है, क्योंकि वो electron-electron repulsion को नज़रअंदाज़ करता है जो तब हावी हो जाता है।

<curious>तो ये check अपने आप होने दीजिए। कोई Bohr formula लगाने से पहले electrons गिनिए। एक electron, और पूरा toolkit आपका। दो या ज़्यादा, और आपको इसे रखना होगा, चाहे साफ़ scalings कितने ललचाएँ। tool कब न इस्तेमाल करें, ये जानना उसे अच्छे से इस्तेमाल करने जितना ही जवाब का हिस्सा है।

board_events.text: Six facts total: three scalings and three anchors. Everything else in this subtopic is a ratio.
For comparison questions, never compute fully. Divide the two cases and let the constants cancel.
Sanity check: any state with $Z = n$ has exactly $-13.6$ eV.
This one pairing of scalings and anchors answers the overwhelming majority of NEET and JEE Main questions in this subtopic in seconds.

segments.text: Let us close Part two the same way we closed Part one, with the single most valuable working habit for the topic. Here it comes down to a small, fixed set of things to memorise, after which almost everything is a ratio.

Memorise three scalings. Radius goes as n squared over Z. Speed goes as Z over n. Energy goes as Z squared over n squared. Look at the panel: three boxes, three scalings, and that is the entire behaviour of the atom compressed into three relationships.

Then memorise three anchors, the ground-state values that turn a scaling into a number. The Bohr radius a nought is zero point five two nine angstroms. The ground-state speed is two point one nine times ten to the sixth metres per second. And the ground-state energy is minus thirteen point six electron volts.

With those six facts, comparison questions become trivial. You are never asked to compute a radius from first principles under time pressure. You are asked how a radius changes between two states, and that is a division in which every constant cancels.
So the rule is: for any comparison, never compute fully. Write the scaling for both cases, divide one by the other, and watch the constants disappear, leaving a clean ratio of the n and Z values.

And keep one sanity check permanently loaded, the one from the N E E T trap earlier. Any state with Z equal to n has an energy of exactly minus thirteen point six electron volts. It is a one-second check that catches a great many slips.
That single pairing, three scalings and three anchors, plus the Z equals n check, answers the overwhelming majority of N E E T and J E E Main questions in this subtopic in seconds, not minutes.

<whisper>So do not leave this subtopic having memorised a dozen full formulas with epsilon noughts and h squareds. Leave it having memorised three scalings, three anchors, and one check. That is the compressed, exam-ready version of everything Bohr gives you, and it is what fast, accurate students actually carry into the hall.
Part दो को उसी तरह ख़त्म करते हैं जैसे Part एक को किया था, topic की सबसे क़ीमती working habit के साथ। यहाँ बात एक छोटे, तय set को रटने पर आ जाती है, जिसके बाद लगभग सब कुछ एक ratio है।

तीन scalings रटिए। radius चलता है n squared over Z की तरह। speed चलती है Z over n की तरह। energy चलती है Z squared over n squared की तरह। panel देखिए: तीन boxes, तीन scalings, और यही atom का पूरा बर्ताव तीन relationships में सिमटा हुआ है।

फिर तीन anchors रटिए, वो ground-state values जो एक scaling को एक number में बदल देती हैं। Bohr radius a nought है zero point five two nine angstroms। ground-state speed है two point one nine times ten to the sixth metres per second। और ground-state energy है माइनस तेरह point छह electron volts।

इन छह facts के साथ comparison सवाल मामूली हो जाते हैं। आपसे कभी वक़्त के दबाव में first principles से radius निकालने को नहीं कहा जाता। पूछा जाता है कि radius दो states के बीच कैसे बदलता है, और वो एक भाग है जिसमें हर constant कट जाता है।
तो नियम है: किसी भी comparison के लिए, पूरा कभी मत गिनिए। दोनों cases के लिए scaling लिखिए, एक को दूसरे से भाग दीजिए, और constants को ग़ायब होते देखिए, पीछे बचता है n और Z values का साफ़ ratio।

और एक sanity check हमेशा लोड रखिए, वही जो पहले N E E T trap से मिला। Z बराबर n वाली किसी भी state की energy बिलकुल माइनस तेरह point छह electron volts होती है। ये एक-सेकंड का check है जो बहुत सारी चूकें पकड़ता है।
वही एक जोड़ी — तीन scalings और तीन anchors, साथ में Z बराबर n वाला check — इस subtopic के ज़्यादातर N E E T और J E E Main सवालों को सेकंडों में जवाब देती है, मिनटों में नहीं।

<whisper>तो इस subtopic को epsilon noughts और h squared वाले दर्जन भर पूरे formulas रटकर मत छोड़िए। इसे तीन scalings, तीन anchors, और एक check रटकर छोड़िए। यही Bohr की दी हर चीज़ का सिमटा, exam-ready रूप है, और यही तेज़, सटीक students असल में hall में ले जाते हैं।
