board_events.text: Scattering: alphas on gold; about 1 in 8000 rebound past $90^\circ$, so the atom is mostly empty with a tiny dense nucleus. $d = 2Ze^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0 K$; $b$ carries $\cot(\theta/2)$; $N \propto 1/\sin^4(\theta/2)$.
Two failures of Rutherford: stability (the electron should spiral in) and spectra (cannot explain sharp lines). Both motivate Bohr.
Bohr: $mvr = nh/2\pi$; $r \propto n^2/Z$, $v \propto Z/n$, $E \propto Z^2/n^2$; anchors $a_0 = 0.529$ \AA, $v_1 = 2.19\times10^{6}$ m/s, $E_1 = -13.6$ eV; valid only for one-electron systems.
Spectra: $1/\lambda = RZ^2(1/n_f^2 - 1/n_i^2)$; series Lyman-UV, Balmer-visible, rest infrared; line count $n(n-1)/2$; series limit $n_f^2/RZ^2$.
Mnemonics: 'Head-on heads back' ($b=0 \Rightarrow \theta=180^\circ$); '$Z=n$ gives $-13.6$'; 'Limit is shortest, first line is longest'; 'Lazy Boys Play Bridge in Patna'.
Anchors worth instant recall: nuclear size $\sim 10^{-15}$ m, atom $\sim 10^{-10}$ m; ionisation of hydrogen 13.6 eV; H-alpha 656 nm; Balmer limit 364.6 nm.

segments.text: And now the chapter cheat sheet, the single card to glance at in the last minutes before the exam. This pulls the whole of Atoms, all three subtopics, into one recall surface. Everything here you have already met and understood; this is pure retrieval practice.

Start with scattering. Alphas fired at gold foil, about one in eight thousand rebounding past ninety degrees, forcing the conclusion that the atom is mostly empty with a tiny, dense nucleus. Closest approach is d equals two Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought K, the impact parameter carries cot of half theta, and the count goes as one over sine to the fourth of half theta.

Then the two failures of Rutherford's model, which every board exam wants named. Stability: the orbiting electron should radiate and spiral into the nucleus. Spectra: the model cannot explain the sharp discrete lines atoms actually emit. Both failures are what motivate the Bohr model.

Now Bohr, in compressed form. The quantisation rule is m v r equals n h over two pi. The three scalings: radius as n squared over Z, speed as Z over n, energy as Z squared over n squared. The three anchors: Bohr radius zero point five two nine angstroms, ground speed two point one nine times ten to the sixth metres per second, ground energy minus thirteen point six electron volts. And the model is valid only for one-electron systems.

Then spectra. The Rydberg formula, one over lambda equals R Z squared times the bracket. The series: Lyman ultraviolet, Balmer visible, and the rest infrared. The line count n times n minus one over two, and the series limit n f squared over R Z squared.

Now the mnemonics, because under pressure these are what actually surface. Head-on heads back, for impact parameter zero giving theta of one hundred and eighty degrees. Z equals n gives minus thirteen point six. Limit is shortest, first line is longest. And Lazy Boys Play Bridge in Patna, for the five series in order.

And a few anchor numbers worth instant recall: the nucleus is about ten to the minus fifteen metres, the atom about ten to the minus ten. Hydrogen's ionisation energy is thirteen point six electron volts, the red H-alpha line is six hundred and fifty six nanometres, and the Balmer limit is three hundred and sixty four point six.

<whisper>That single card is the whole chapter, compressed to what you can scan in the final minutes. If every line triggers the understanding beneath it, you are ready. That is the end of the Atoms chapter, and you now hold all of it, from the first scattering alpha to the last spectral line of hydrogen, as one connected picture.

और अब chapter cheat sheet, वो इकलौता card जिसे exam से ठीक पहले आख़िरी मिनटों में देखना है। ये पूरे Atoms को, तीनों subtopics को, एक recall सतह पर खींच लाता है। यहाँ सब कुछ आप पहले ही मिल और समझ चुके हैं; ये शुद्ध retrieval अभ्यास है।

scattering से शुरू कीजिए। gold foil पर दागे alpha particles, करीब आठ हज़ार में एक नब्बे degrees से ज़्यादा मुड़कर, जो ये निष्कर्ष मजबूर करता है कि atom ज़्यादातर खाली जगह है एक छोटे, dense nucleus के साथ। closest approach है d बराबर two Z e squared over four pi epsilon nought K, impact parameter half theta का cotangent रखता है, और scattering count चलता है one over sine to the fourth of half theta की तरह।

फिर Rutherford के model की दो failures, जिन्हें हर board exam नाम से चाहता है। stability: orbit करता electron radiate करके nucleus में spiral हो जाना चाहिए। spectra: model उन तेज़ discrete lines को नहीं समझा सकता जो atoms सचमुच छोड़ते हैं। दोनों failures ही Bohr model को प्रेरित करती हैं।

अब Bohr, सिमटे रूप में। quantisation rule है m v r बराबर n h over two pi। तीन scalings: radius n squared over Z की तरह, speed Z over n की तरह, energy Z squared over n squared की तरह। तीन anchors: Bohr radius zero point five two nine angstroms, ground speed two point one nine times ten to the sixth metres per second, ground energy माइनस तेरह point छह electron volts। और model सिर्फ़ one-electron systems के लिए valid है।

फिर spectra। Rydberg formula, one over lambda बराबर R Z squared गुणा bracket। series: Lyman ultraviolet, Balmer visible, और बाक़ी infrared। line count n गुणा n माइनस एक बटा दो, और series limit n f squared over R Z squared।

अब mnemonics, क्योंकि दबाव में यही असल में याद आते हैं। Head-on heads back, impact parameter zero से theta एक सौ अस्सी degrees के लिए। Z बराबर n देता है माइनस तेरह point छह। Limit is shortest, first line is longest। और Lazy Boys Play Bridge in Patna, पाँच series के क्रम के लिए।

और कुछ anchor numbers तुरंत याद रखने लायक़: nucleus करीब दस की घात माइनस पंद्रह metres, atom करीब दस की घात माइनस दस। hydrogen की ionisation energy तेरह point छह electron volts, लाल H-alpha line छह सौ छप्पन nanometres, और Balmer limit तीन सौ चौंसठ point छह।
